note: The First Bulgarian Empire (founded 681 by Asparuh Khan) competed with Byzantium for dominance over the Balkans for 340 years. Major conflicts included: Avar-Bulgarian pressure on Constantinople (811–813), Khan Krum's destruction of the Byzantine army at Pliska (811, killing Emperor Nikephoros I in the only emperor killed in battle since 378), the conversion of Boris I (864), the Bulgarian-Byzantine war under Simeon I (who besieged Constantinople three times), and Basil II's systematic conquest culminating in Kleidion (1014). The rivalry defined the political character of the medieval Balkans.

_quarry.structural_significance: The first Bulgarian-Byzantine rivalry defines the fundamental Balkan political dynamic: two imperial powers competing for the same Orthodox Christian population and the same strategic territory; the Bulgarian threat repeatedly forces Byzantium to make concessions (Boris's conversion on favorable terms, recognition of the Bulgarian patriarchate) that shaped Orthodox Christianity's Slavic expansion
